solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Netting used in game show

indicators.note: the letters are used within the run of the words game show, so the answer sits inside them

explanation.surface: Some netting is a prop in a television quiz programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesh is open-weave material, the stuff a net is made from, so it is a synonym for netting.

clue.text: A wife, after lively dances, brings out puzzle

indicators.note: the A and wife piece is placed after the dances piece

parts.note: jigs are brisk folk dances

explanation.surface: After some energetic dancing, a married woman gets out a puzzle to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a picture puzzle cut into interlocking pieces to be reassembled.

clue.text: River Trent's banks?

definitions.meaning: a river of north-east England flowing out at Middlesbrough
the outer letters, or banks, of the word Trent are two Ts, and the plural of the letter name T is spelt this way

explanation.walkthrough: The surface invokes the English river Trent, but its banks here are its first and last letters, written out as letter names.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a river in north-east England, flowing to the North Sea at Teesside.

clue.text: Pottery in Russian vehicle

definitions.meaning: ... Pottery was a Cornish studio pottery making distinctive ceramics from 1963 to 1983
a Russian carriage or sleigh drawn by three horses abreast

explanation.walkthrough: The pottery sense is a proper name: Troika ware came from a studio in St Ives and later Newlyn, Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian sleigh or carriage pulled by a team of three horses side by side.

clue.text: Rebound causing defender to shoot

parts.note: in football a back is a defensive player
to fire is to shoot a gun

explanation.surface: A footballer sees a defender take a shot that bounces back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebound' is a verb here: a plan that backfires rebounds on its maker.
explanation.definitionFit: To backfire is to have the opposite effect to that intended, recoiling on the person responsible.

clue.text: Conservative writer? Correct

parts.note: blue is the colour of the British Conservative Party, so a Tory is a blue
a pencil is something one writes with

explanation.surface: A Tory author is told to put things right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct' is a verb: editors traditionally marked cuts and corrections in blue pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue-pencil is to edit or censor text, marking errors and cuts for amendment.

clue.text: Rather inferior wine I bottled, rouge with no body

indicators.note: the wine holds the I as a bottle holds its contents

parts.note: Medoc is a red Bordeaux wine

indicators.note: the middle of the word rouge is dropped, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rather poor red is described as having no body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no body' leaves RE, the ends of rouge, after MEDIOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mediocre is of only moderate or second-rate quality, a little below par.

clue.text: Legal precedents about part of UK to the north

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Wales is one of the four nations of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A ruling on legal history concerns some northerly area of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' turns WALES into SELAW, read upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Case law is the body of law built up from judges' earlier decisions, used as precedents.

clue.text: Band together once more? No kidding

definitions.meaning: to ally again, read as ..., is to join forces a second time
an interjection of surprise or emphasis meaning is that so

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the answer into RE (again) and ALLY (band together), hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an exclamation, it expresses surprise or disbelief, just like saying no kidding.

clue.text: Spirits supplied by good landlords

parts.note: a landlord of a pub is its host

explanation.surface: The publicans provide the alcohol in their pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirits look like drink served by landlords, but they are phantoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts are spectres of the dead, which is one sense of spirits.

clue.text: Singular person who amuses perfectionist

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a tickler is someone who tickles, that is amuses or entertains

explanation.surface: An odd comedian turns out to be a fusspot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' seems to mean odd or peculiar, but it only gives the abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exact standards in every detail, the hallmark of a perfectionist.

clue.text: Book a week in it, local resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday advert suggests a week at a nearby seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday destination, but read as re-sort it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Town Like Alice is Nevil Shute's 1950 novel, partly set in the Australian outback.

clue.text: Stolen jewellery? Nonsense

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang jewellery is called tom, and stolen goods are tom too, from the rhyme with jewellery

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang uses the full word as a rhyme for jewellery, so a thief's loot of jewels can be described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomfoolery is silly, foolish behaviour, synonymous with nonsense or horseplay.

clue.text: Latest in dock 19 is a two-master

indicators.note: the last letter of the word dock is taken

parts.note: the answer to 19 across, meaning to carve

explanation.surface: The newest boat to arrive at the harbour has two masts.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' refers to the entry 19 across, whose answer is reused as a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketch is a sailing boat with two masts, the mizzen set forward of the rudder.

clue.text: Woodhouse or Wodehouse finally married academic

indicators.note: only the last letter of the name Wodehouse is used

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is an academic degree, standing for its holder

explanation.surface: A novelist, Austen's or P G Wodehouse's, ends up wed to a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: The near-identical names mislead: Woodhouse is the surname of an Austen heroine, and Wodehouse is the comic novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel named after her.

clue.text: Cure if I don't eat is useless

indicators.note: the letters are no use in their present order, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dieter's remedy fails because they will not eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is useless' is the anagram signal on I DON'T EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that counteracts a poison, a kind of cure.

clue.text: Head of coven enters accompanied by hag

indicators.note: the coven piece goes into the accompanied piece

parts.note: with means accompanied by

indicators.note: the first letter of the word coven is taken

explanation.surface: The leader of a witches' gathering arrives with an old crone.
explanation.walkthrough: C, the head of coven, enters WITH.
explanation.definitionFit: A hag is an ugly old woman, and in folklore specifically a witch.

clue.text: Old man, leader of Hallé and American orchestra

indicators.note: the first letter of the name Hallé is taken

parts.note: US stands for the United States, so for American
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: An elderly conductor directs the Hallé and an American orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hallé is a Manchester orchestra; 'Old man' is informal British for a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: My old man is colloquial British for one's husband or male partner.

clue.text: Some basket chairs, etc, hard to carve

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the run of words are used

explanation.surface: Some wicker furniture is hard to whittle.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in fact hidden twice: in basket chairs and again in etc, hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave a design by cutting into a surface, a form of carving.

clue.text: Coming from where we do is wonderful?

definitions.meaning: taken literally, the phrase describes something from beyond our own planet
an idiom for superb or marvellous

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading treats the idiom literally: away from the planet we come from.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something so excellent it seems beyond earthly standards, hence marvellous.

clue.text: Colours on bottle

parts.note: a regiment's colours are its flag
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flag is attached to a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large bottle or jug for wine or cider.

clue.text: Player, one wearing odd boots

indicators.note: the scrambled boots are worn around the one
odd means peculiar, so the letters are put in a strange order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A musician turns up in mismatched footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' turns BOOTS into OBOST, and 'wearing' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, so is a player in an orchestra.

clue.text: Jokes about boy, last to wear dressy clothes

indicators.note: the jokes piece goes around the other pieces

parts.note: gags are jokes
a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the final letter of the word wear is taken

explanation.surface: Jokes are made about a young man who is last to put on smart clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to wear' gives the final letter R, not a sense of being the last person to dress; 'about' wraps the jokes round both the boy and that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal phrase for one's best clothes worn for a special occasion.

clue.text: Belt found in small wood

parts.note: ash is a timber from the ash tree

explanation.surface: A belt is discovered in a little copse.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn round the waist or over the shoulder, like a belt.

clue.text: Immediately pay the penalty, catching cold

indicators.note: the atone piece catches and holds the cold piece

parts.note: to atone is to make amends for a wrong

explanation.surface: Someone must pay a fine straight away for having caught a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts C inside ATONE.
explanation.definitionFit: At once is an idiom meaning without delay, straight away.

clue.text: Chapter about origin of wedding band

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the first letter of the word wedding is taken

explanation.surface: A book chapter tells of the beginnings of a wedding band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a ring or musicians at a wedding, but it is a team of workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a group of people working together, a band or gang.

clue.text: See rubbish leading to cave

indicators.note: the rubbish piece comes first, leading the word to

parts.note: grot is informal British for rubbish or junk
taken as written

explanation.surface: Look at the junk at the entrance of a cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: GROT is British slang for rubbish; 'See' is just a lead-in instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave, natural or artificial.

clue.text: Avoid team that has upset favourites

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

indicators.note: upset in a down sense means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pets are favourites, as a teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Dodge a squad that has beaten the bookmakers' favourites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like a sporting shock, but it turns PETS into STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep is to evade or dodge something, literally by stepping aside.
